newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq's Uday in better health Qatari visitors say.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Uday in better health Qatari visitors say.

text.p: A Qatari delegation who visited Iraq President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday, who was shot last year, said his health was "better", the influential newspaper Babel said on Sunday.

Babel said that chairman of the Qatari Ta'wan (cooperation) football club Sheikh Khalifa Ben Ahmed al Thani visited Uday for the third time since he was wounded by unidentified gunmen while driving in Baghdad on December 12.
"We have come to be assured of your health and thank God we have seen you in a better condition," Babel, owned by Uday, quoted Thani as saying.
Shabab television, also owned by Uday, on Saturday showed him shaking hands and kissing the Qatari delegation while lying in his hospital bed in Baghdad.
Iraq blamed a pro-Iranian group for the attack and has urged the U.N. to press Iran to hand over the attackers. Iranian officials have denied the charges.
Uday is chairman of Iraq's National Olympic Committee.
